value.body: A risk analyst estimates how much a bank, lender or investment firm could lose, and helps keep that within limits. Employers include banks, NBFCs, fintech lenders, global banks' analytics centres and consultancies. A typical day involves working with large datasets, running or validating statistical models, and preparing reports for risk committees.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Stat, B.Math, statistics, economics or engineering graduates

items.label: Common areas
items.value: Credit risk, market risk, model validation

items.label: NBFCs registered with RBI
items.note: Down from ~9,400 in March 2023 as registrations were cancelled
items.source: RBI data cited in a law-firm sector paper (as reported)

items.label: NBFC sector balance sheet
items.source: RBI Report on Trend and Progress of Banking in India 2024-25 (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join through campus hiring or analyst programmes at banks and analytics firms, often after a test on statistics, probability and coding. Professional risk certifications are often taken later on the job.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Programming in Python, R or SAS

value.title: At a glance
items: Work is closely tied to banking regulation and audit requirements.
Next roles: senior risk analyst, model developer, risk manager.
